paper.title: Efficient Uncoupled Learning Dynamics with $\tilde{O}\!\left(T^{-1/4}\right)$ Last-Iterate Convergence in Bilinear Saddle-Point Problems over Convex Sets under Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Last-iterate convergence in bilinear saddle-point problems over compact convex sets under bandit feedback (self-play)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in two-player zero-sum games with a Nash-equilibrium (last-iterate convergence) objective under self-play.
unmapped: two-player zero-sum bilinear game <x, A y> with both players running uncoupled dynamics (self-play)
objective: the iterate (x_k, y_k) is an eps_k-approximate Nash equilibrium (last-iterate convergence)
uncoupled: players observe neither the opponent's actions nor its action set or dimension
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal{X} \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $\mathcal{Y} \subset \mathbb{R}^{m}$ be compact, convex sets, and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}$ be an input matrix. We assume $\mathrm{span}(\mathcal{X}) = \mathbb{R}^{n}$ ... $\langle x, Ay \rangle \in [-1,1]$ ... In each round $k$, the row player selects $x_k \in \mathcal{X}$ and the column player selects $y_k \in \mathcal{Y}$. They then receive standard bandit feedback in the form of $\langle x_k, Ay_k \rangle$ and $-\langle x_k, Ay_k \rangle$, respectively.

algorithms.name: Last-iterate algorithm under bandit feedback (phased OFTRL with experimental-design exploration and ellipsoid regularizer)

symbols.n_dim: dimension of the row player's action set X
symbols.m_dim: dimension of the column player's action set Y
symbols.T: round index k at which the Nash gap eps_k of the iterate (x_k,y_k) is measured

conditions: X, Y compact convex, spanning R^n and R^m
<x, A y> in [-1,1] for all x in X, y in Y

source.label: thm:main_theorem
source.quote: Let $(x_k, y_k)$ denote the iterates generated by the two players running Algorithm~\ref{algo:last_iter_bandit_feedback} with step size $\eta = \tfrac{1}{6}$ in each round $k$. Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for every $k \geq 1$, the iterate $(x_k,y_k)$ is an $\varepsilon_k$-approximate Nash equilibrium, where $\varepsilon_k = \mathrm{poly}(n,m,\log(k/\delta)) \, k^{-1/4}$.

results.notes: The theorem itself states eps_k = poly(n,m,log(k/delta)) k^{-1/4}. The explicit polynomial is the one derived at the end of Section 3. The quantity is the Nash-equilibrium gap of the last iterate, not regret. Polynomial time requires linear optimization oracles for the action sets.
